_note: Source for tools/generate-advisory.mjs → advisory/slides/orientation-{student,parent}.html. Standalone — no course page. Teacher bio, email, room, and the executive-function moves are pulled from calendar/orientation.json `shared` so they stay in sync with the course decks. SEL themes are internal; the year arc here is deliberately generic.

what: Executive function — the habits that make the year work
Ice breakers, circles, and the occasional game

jobs.d: I am your liaison to every teacher, coach, and office in the high school. Ask me first.
Twice a week we do the work no other class has time for: how you are doing, and how to handle it.
Planner, notes, sleep, starting early. Practised here daily until they are yours.

askMe: Can I switch out of a class?
A teacher marked me absent and I was there.
Where do I actually eat lunch?
I have three tests on Thursday.
How do I start a club?
I do not get along with my lab partner.

roles.for: Anything. Schedules, people, clubs, sports, a bad week. I route you to the right person and follow up.
A grade, an assignment, a makeup. Email them first — copy me if it is not getting solved.
Bigger than a bad week. I will walk you there myself.
Attendance, discipline, the handbook. I am usually in the conversation.
Course placement, big-picture decisions. Go through me first.

arc.d: Routines, the planner, sleep, the building. Get your feet under you.
Stress, first exams, asking for help before it compounds.
Friendships, conflict, who you are becoming here.
Reflection, course choices, what sophomore-you will thank you for.

norms.t: What is said here stays here
norms.d: The one rule that makes the rest possible.
Late to advisory is late to school.

firstWeek: Veracross login works — check tonight, not Monday
Read your schedule: A days, B days, single-period Mondays
Find Room 503. Then find your locker
Charger in the bag, every day
One planner or notebook for every class
Learn two names you did not know yesterday

iceBreakers.d: The classic. I go first and mine are hard.
Sixty seconds, any question from the room. Pass allowed, once.
Pin where you live, where you eat, where you would take a visitor.
One song each, no vetoes. It plays every morning at 8:00.
Name, plus one thing you are weirdly good at. Demos encouraged.
Three things. Defend them. No phones allowed on the island.

rituals.d: Someone did something good this week. Say it out loud.
Your day, your song on the playlist, your pick of the weather icon.
One big question on the board all month. Answers go on the wall.

memes.top: Freshman year: I will have high school figured out by September
memes.bottom: September: learning which staircase goes where
memes.caption: Nobody has it figured out in September. That is what the room is for.

memes.top: Me: you can ask me literally anything
memes.bottom: First question: what is the wifi password
memes.caption: Still counts. Ask the next one too.

memes.top: Me at 7:58 with a cold brew, ready to be your advisor
memes.caption: 8:00 means 8:00. The elevator is not a reason.

useMe.t: Email me first for anything non-academic
useMe.d: Schedules, social stuff, a rough week, a question you do not know who to ask. I route it and follow up.

useMe.t: Email the teacher first for a grade
useMe.d: Copy me. If it is not getting solved in a week, I step in.

useMe.t: Tell me what I cannot see
useMe.d: Sleep, a move, a loss, a new sibling. Context changes how I read a bad Tuesday.
School days. Friday emails get a Monday reply.

notThis.d: When something is bigger than a bad week, I walk your student to the counselor myself — and I tell you.
I can see grades and I will flag patterns, but the teacher owns the gradebook.

notThis.t: Not a substitute for the handbook
notThis.d: Attendance and discipline live with the dean. I am usually in the room for the conversation.

atHome.d: Sunny, cloudy, storm, hurricane? It is the same check-in we do at 8:00, and it gets more than 'fine'.
Ninth graders who sleep eight hours do better in every class I teach. Phones out of the bedroom.
Ask to see it; do not fill it in. The habit only sticks if they own it.

atHome.t: Let a small thing go wrong
atHome.d: A forgotten charger in September is the cheapest lesson they will ever get.
